# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print a library shelf list. Fields are separated by a vertical bar (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `dots`, `heavy` (see below) | `dots` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dots` | `o` | `_` | `:` | `=` |
| `heavy` | `.` | `_` | `:` | `~` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `o_____o___o`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `src/boxtab.sh` (run as `bash src/boxtab.sh`; bash 5 and the usual POSIX tools such as awk and sed are available).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
|anchor reef|ferry
pier|1394|oar brine
73.50|mast|tide
EOF
o_______o_____________o___________o
:       : anchor reef : ferry     :
o=======o=============o===========o
: pier  : 1394        : oar brine :
: 73.50 : mast        : tide      :
o_______o_____________o___________o
```

```
$ boxtab style=heavy header=no <<'EOF'
pier|80|4250
anchor sail|lantern|ferry
249.19|2230|swell net
3638|84.70|1894
EOF
._____________._________.___________.
: pier        : 80      : 4250      :
: anchor sail : lantern : ferry     :
: 249.19      : 2230    : swell net :
: 3638        : 84.70   : 1894      :
```

start.README.md:
# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print an allotment rota. Fields are separated by a comma (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `tilde`, `plain` (see below) | `tilde` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tilde` | `#` | `=` | `|` | `~` |
| `plain` | `*` | `~` | `I` | `#` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `#=====#===#`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `src/boxtab.py` (run as `python3 src/boxtab.py`).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
,quay,
3160,kelp oar,
lantern,1085,950
EOF
#=========#==========#=====#
|         | quay     |     |
#~~~~~~~~~#~~~~~~~~~~#~~~~~#
| 3160    | kelp oar |     |
| lantern | 1085     | 950 |
#=========#==========#=====#
```

```
$ boxtab style=plain header=no <<'EOF'
harbour,dock,4871
93.16,sail swell,harbour sail
moor tide,1254,3604
harbour oar,pier dock,oar
EOF
*~~~~~~~~~~~~~*~~~~~~~~~~~~*~~~~~~~~~~~~~~*
I harbour     I dock       I 4871         I
I 93.16       I sail swell I harbour sail I
I moor tide   I 1254       I 3604         I
I harbour oar I pier dock  I oar          I
*~~~~~~~~~~~~~*~~~~~~~~~~~~*~~~~~~~~~~~~~~*
```

```
$ boxtab style=plain header=no <<'EOF'
4189,4688
oar swell,salt buoy
gull,sail kelp
EOF
*~~~~~~~~~~~*~~~~~~~~~~~*
I 4189      I 4688      I
I oar swell I salt buoy I
I gull      I sail kelp I
*~~~~~~~~~~~*~~~~~~~~~~~*
```

# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print the tide log. Fields are separated by a vertical bar (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `dots`, `plain`, `ascii` (see below) | `dots` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |
| `align` | a non-empty string of letters, one per column from the left: `l` left, `r` right, `c` centre; columns beyond the string are `l`, letters beyond the last column are ignored | all `l` |
| `pad` | `0`, `1`, `2` or `3`: spaces on each side of a cell | `1` |

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dots` | `*` | `-` | `I` | `=` |
| `plain` | `+` | `=` | `|` | `~` |
| `ascii` | `#` | `_` | `I` | `#` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `*-----*---*`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `src/main.c` (plus any other `.c` files under `src/`; built with `gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra`).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
1820|88.82|2484
lantern|pier buoy|2861
2993|moor|brine anchor
EOF
*---------*-----------*--------------*
I 1820    I 88.82     I 2484         I
*=========*===========*==============*
I lantern I pier buoy I 2861         I
I 2993    I moor      I brine anchor I
*---------*-----------*--------------*
```

```
$ boxtab style=ascii align=lrc <<'EOF'
248.04|725|mast
salt|harbour pier|3696
4643|moor|swell
reef reef|406|3317
EOF
#___________#______________#_______#
I 248.04    I          725 I mast  I
####################################
I salt      I harbour pier I 3696  I
I 4643      I         moor I swell I
I reef reef I          406 I 3317  I
#___________#______________#_______#
```

```
$ boxtab style=plain header=no pad=2 <<'EOF'
net|oar
tide lantern|brine
105.68|4473
EOF
+================+=========+
|  net           |  oar    |
|  tide lantern  |  brine  |
|  105.68        |  4473   |
+================+=========+
```

# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print a ferry timetable. Fields are separated by a semicolon (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `tilde`, `stars`, `heavy` (see below) | `tilde` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |
| `align` | a non-empty string of letters, one per column from the left: `l` left, `r` right, `c` centre; columns beyond the string are `l`, letters beyond the last column are ignored | all `l` |
| `pad` | `0`, `1`, `2` or `3`: spaces on each side of a cell | `1` |

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `tilde` | `.` | `-` | `I` | `=` |
| `stars` | `o` | `.` | `I` | `=` |
| `heavy` | `.` | `-` | `:` | `=` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `.-----.---.`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `main.go` and any other `.go` files in the module root (package `main`; built with `go build -o build/boxtab .`).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
870;2310;2673
;1554;147.76
gull;3706;3421
EOF
.------.------.--------.
I 870  I 2310 I 2673   I
.======.======.========.
I      I 1554 I 147.76 I
I gull I 3706 I 3421   I
.------.------.--------.
```

```
$ boxtab style=heavy align=lrc <<'EOF'
364;176.26;pier
brine reef;168.58;4575
106.90;reef sail;2322
191.79;salt;harbour
EOF
.------------.-----------.---------.
: 364        :    176.26 :  pier   :
.============.===========.=========.
: brine reef :    168.58 :  4575   :
: 106.90     : reef sail :  2322   :
: 191.79     :      salt : harbour :
.------------.-----------.---------.
```

```
$ boxtab style=stars header=no pad=2 <<'EOF'
reef;4802
141.43;sail
312;
EOF
o..........o........o
I  reef    I  4802  I
I  141.43  I  sail  I
I  312     I        I
o..........o........o
```

# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print a ferry timetable. Fields are separated by a tab (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `dots`, `plain`, `thin` (see below) | `dots` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |
| `align` | a non-empty string of letters, one per column from the left: `l` left, `r` right, `c` centre, `n` numeric (see below); columns beyond the string are `l`, letters beyond the last column are ignored | all `l` |
| `pad` | `0`, `1`, `2` or `3`: spaces on each side of a cell | `1` |
| `max` | an integer from 2 to 99 written with one or two ASCII digits (no sign) | no limit |
| `rules` | `edges` or `all` | `edges` |

**`max=N`**: a cell longer than `N` characters is replaced by its first `N-1` characters followed by `~` (so its length becomes `N`). This is done before the column widths are computed.

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dots` | `#` | `_` | `!` | `~` |
| `plain` | `.` | `=` | `|` | `#` |
| `thin` | `+` | `.` | `|` | `-` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `#_____#___#`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length). `n` means: right-aligned when the cell is *numeric* - an optional `+` or `-`, one or more ASCII digits, optionally `.` and one or more digits - and left-aligned otherwise (decided cell by cell).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`, and after every other row except the last a rule with `h` if `rules=all`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `src/boxtab.sh` (run as `bash src/boxtab.sh`; bash 5 and the usual POSIX tools such as awk and sed are available).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
1791<TAB>193.53<TAB>2665
pier<TAB>3483<TAB>47.83
anchor<TAB>dock swell<TAB>3422
EOF
#________#____________#_______#
! 1791   ! 193.53     ! 2665  !
#~~~~~~~~#~~~~~~~~~~~~#~~~~~~~#
! pier   ! 3483       ! 47.83 !
! anchor ! dock swell ! 3422  !
#________#____________#_______#
```

```
$ boxtab style=thin align=lrc <<'EOF'
oar<TAB>214.25<TAB>2711
2648<TAB>765<TAB>gull
101.09<TAB><TAB>brine oar
33.28<TAB>reef<TAB>321
EOF
+........+........+...........+
| oar    | 214.25 |   2711    |
+--------+--------+-----------+
| 2648   |    765 |   gull    |
| 101.09 |        | brine oar |
| 33.28  |   reef |    321    |
+........+........+...........+
```

```
$ boxtab style=plain header=no pad=2 <<'EOF'
202.25<TAB>289.61
2130<TAB>
4689<TAB>pier
EOF
.==========.==========.
|  202.25  |  289.61  |
|  2130    |          |
|  4689    |  pier    |
.==========.==========.
```

(`<TAB>` stands for a tab character in the examples above.)

# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print an allotment rota. Fields are separated by a semicolon (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `dots`, `thin`, `heavy` (see below) | `dots` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |
| `align` | a non-empty string of letters, one per column from the left: `l` left, `r` right, `c` centre, `n` numeric (see below); columns beyond the string are `l`, letters beyond the last column are ignored | all `l` |
| `pad` | `0`, `1`, `2` or `3`: spaces on each side of a cell | `1` |
| `max` | an integer from 2 to 99 written with one or two ASCII digits (no sign) | no limit |
| `rules` | `edges` or `all` | `edges` |

**`max=N`**: a cell longer than `N` characters is replaced by its first `N-1` characters followed by `~` (so its length becomes `N`). This is done before the column widths are computed.

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dots` | `.` | `~` | `|` | `-` |
| `thin` | `.` | `.` | `!` | `=` |
| `heavy` | `o` | `.` | `:` | `#` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `.~~~~~.~~~.`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length). `n` means: right-aligned when the cell is *numeric* - an optional `+` or `-`, one or more ASCII digits, optionally `.` and one or more digits - and left-aligned otherwise (decided cell by cell).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`, and after every other row except the last a rule with `h` if `rules=all`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `src/main.c` (plus any other `.c` files under `src/`; built with `gcc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra`).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
1086;lantern;193.83
dock;4781;3210
1636;4785;net
EOF
```

start.README.md:
# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print a lamp inventory. Fields are separated by a semicolon (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `thin`, `ascii`, `dots` (see below) | `thin` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |
| `align` | a non-empty string of letters, one per column from the left: `l` left, `r` right, `c` centre; columns beyond the string are `l`, letters beyond the last column are ignored | all `l` |
| `pad` | `0`, `1`, `2` or `3`: spaces on each side of a cell | `1` |

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `thin` | `+` | `=` | `!` | `#` |
| `ascii` | `+` | `=` | `:` | `~` |
| `dots` | `o` | `=` | `!` | `~` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `+=====+===+`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `main.go` and any other `.go` files in the module root (package `main`; built with `go build -o build/boxtab .`).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
;brine;227.05
290.09;kelp;anchor salt
;3214;tide dock
EOF
+========+=======+=============+
!        ! brine ! 227.05      !
+########+#######+#############+
! 290.09 ! kelp  ! anchor salt !
!        ! 3214  ! tide dock   !
+========+=======+=============+
```

```
$ boxtab style=dots align=lrc <<'EOF'
reef;4015;salt gull
4953;;
3172;2463;76.19
buoy;56;56.49
EOF
o======o======o===========o
! reef ! 4015 ! salt gull !
o~~~~~~o~~~~~~o~~~~~~~~~~~o
! 4953 !      !           !
! 3172 ! 2463 !   76.19   !
! buoy !   56 !   56.49   !
o======o======o===========o
```

```
$ boxtab style=ascii header=no pad=2 <<'EOF'
oar reef;swell pier
harbour;harbour
swell;oar
EOF
+============+==============+
:  oar reef  :  swell pier  :
:  harbour   :  harbour     :
:  swell     :  oar         :
+============+==============+
```

# boxtab: tables for plain text

`boxtab` reads delimited text on standard input and prints it as a bordered table. The office uses it to print a lamp inventory. Fields are separated by a tab (no quoting: a field can never contain the separator). Options are given as command-line arguments of the form `key=value`.

## Input

Lines end with `\n`; if the input ends with `\n`, that last newline is not a row separator (it is simply removed first). If nothing is left, there are no rows: print nothing and exit with status 1. Otherwise each remaining line is a row, empty lines included (an empty line is a row with one empty cell). Each row is split at every separator, so `a,,b` has three cells, the middle one empty and a row ending in a separator ends with an empty cell. The table has as many columns as the longest row; shorter rows are padded on the right with empty cells. Cells are plain ASCII text (anything except the separator and newline).

## Options

Every argument must be exactly one option `key=value`; each key may be used at most once, and only the keys below exist. Any violation (an argument without `=`, an unknown or repeated key, an invalid value, a key that this version does not have) makes the program print nothing to standard output, write a message to standard error and exit with status 2 -- before standard input is looked at.

| key | values | default |
|---|---|---|
| `style` | `ascii`, `tilde`, `plain` (see below) | `ascii` |
| `header` | `yes` or `no` | `yes` |
| `align` | a non-empty string of letters, one per column from the left: `l` left, `r` right, `c` centre, `n` numeric (see below); columns beyond the string are `l`, letters beyond the last column are ignored | all `l` |
| `pad` | `0`, `1`, `2` or `3`: spaces on each side of a cell | `1` |
| `max` | an integer from 2 to 99 written with one or two ASCII digits (no sign) | no limit |
| `rules` | `edges` or `all` | `edges` |

**`max=N`**: a cell longer than `N` characters is replaced by its first `N-1` characters followed by `~` (so its length becomes `N`). This is done before the column widths are computed.

## Drawing

The *width* of a column is the length of its longest cell (0 if all its cells are empty). Each style has four characters, `corner`, `h` (horizontal), `v` (vertical) and `hh` (the horizontal character of the header rule):

| style | corner | h | v | hh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ascii` | `.` | `=` | `I` | `#` |
| `tilde` | `*` | `-` | `|` | `=` |
| `plain` | `+` | `_` | `|` | `-` |

A **rule** is `corner`, then for every column `(width + 2*pad)` copies of the rule's horizontal character followed by `corner`: for two columns of widths 3 and 1 and `pad=1`, with the first style's characters, it is `.=====.===.`. A **row line** is `v`, then for every column `pad` spaces, the cell aligned inside `width` characters, `pad` spaces and `v`.

Alignment inside the column: `l` puts the cell first and fills with spaces, `r` puts the spaces first, `c` puts `floor(room/2)` spaces before and the rest after (`room` = width minus cell length). `n` means: right-aligned when the cell is *numeric* - an optional `+` or `-`, one or more ASCII digits, optionally `.` and one or more digits - and left-aligned otherwise (decided cell by cell).

The output is: a rule with `h`; then the rows in order, where after the **first** row there is a rule with `hh` if `header=yes`, and after every other row except the last a rule with `h` if `rules=all`; and finally a rule with `h`. Every line, including the last, ends with `\n`. A table with a single row and `header=yes` therefore has two rules after the row (the `hh` rule, then the closing rule).

Exit status: 0 after printing a table, 1 when there are no rows, 2 for an option error.

## Where

The program lives in `src/boxtab.sh` (run as `bash src/boxtab.sh`; bash 5 and the usual POSIX tools such as awk and sed are available).

## Examples

```
$ boxtab <<'EOF'
1284<TAB>sail dock<TAB>sail lantern
621<TAB>2456<TAB>dock kelp
<TAB>10.85<TAB>2191
EOF
.======.===========.==============.
I 1284 I sail dock I sail lantern I
.######.###########.##############.
I 621  I 2456      I dock kelp    I
I      I 10.85     I 2191         I
.======.===========.==============.
```

```
$ boxtab style=plain align=lrc <<'EOF'
pier mast<TAB>gull mast<TAB>oar
1789<TAB>brine<TAB>swell quay
2191<TAB>4844<TAB>
harbour<TAB>quay swell<TAB>swell
EOF
+___________+____________+____________+
| pier mast |  gull mast |    oar     |
+-----------+------------+------------+
| 1789      |      brine | swell quay |
| 2191      |       4844 |            |
| harbour   | quay swell |   swell    |
+___________+____________+____________+
```

```
$ boxtab style=tilde header=no pad=2 <<'EOF'
2600<TAB>2804
<TAB>
sail<TAB>pier
EOF
*--------*--------*
|  2600  |  2804  |
|        |        |
|  sail  |  pier  |
*--------*--------*
```

(`<TAB>` stands for a tab character in the examples above.)
